pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 12.4.1: SHORT STORY: CHARACTERS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What qualities do you admire in people?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the characters in the short story
2. write a paragraph on the characters in the short story
3. appreciate the role of characters in stories

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 12.4.1: SHORT STORY: CHARACTERS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 12.4.1: SHORT STORY: CHARACTERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the characters in the short story

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the characters in the short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the characters in the short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the characters in the short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a paragraph on the characters in the short story

What this means
In this part you learn to write a paragraph on the characters in the short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a paragraph on the characters in the short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a paragraph on the characters in the short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of characters in stories

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of characters in stories. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of characters in stories.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of characters in stories. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the characters in the short story)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters to a partner. (skill: write a paragraph on the characters in the short story)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of characters in stories)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the characters in the short story.
3. Practise this skill: write a paragraph on the characters in the short story.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of characters in stories.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What qualities do you admire in people?
2. How can character traits be described?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the characters in the short story.
5. Be able to: write a paragraph on the characters in the short story.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
